title_original: ART SG Returns for Fifth Edition in January 2027
excerpt_original: The fair will showcase an increasingly global line-up of leading galleries alongside major artist projects and new public programs. Partnership with ART SG

blocks.text: Sponsored
ART SG Returns for Fifth Edition in January 2027

blocks.alt: ART SG Returns for Fifth Edition in January 2027

blocks.text: ART SG returns to Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention from January 22–24, 2027 (VIP Preview and Vernissage on January 21), marking its fifth edition alongside the 15th anniversary of Singapore Art Week. S.E.A. Focus will return for its ninth edition alongside ART SG for a second year of collaboration, featuring a curated selection of galleries from across Southeast Asia that brings the region’s established and emerging artistic positions into focus under the overarching theme “Better Worlds.” Featuring over 110 galleries from more than 30 countries and territories, ART SG and S.E.A. Focus connect Southeast Asia with the international art world, fostering cross-cultural dialogue while showcasing the diversity of contemporary artistic practices from the region.

Notable international names will return to ART SG, presented by Founding and Lead Partner UBS, in 2027 to present highlights from their distinguished programs, including White Cube (London, Hong Kong, Paris, Seoul, New York); Thaddaeus Ropac (London, Salzburg, Paris, Pantin, Seoul, Milan); Galerie Gisela Capitain (Cologne, Naples); neugerriemschneider (Berlin); Galerie Gmurzynska (Zurich, New York); Galerie Urs Meile (Zurich, Beijing, Ardez); Ota Fine Arts (Singapore, Shanghai, Tokyo); and Asia Art Center (Taipei, Beijing).
ARIN SUNARYO ,
Erupturapytch Ag 47 (Tephraic ) #2, 2024, volcanic ash, pigmented resin, and silver chrome mounted on wooden panel, 314 x 197 x 5.5 cm (diptych). Courtesy Gajah Gallery.
TOMAS SARACENO ,
Altocumulus Albus Opacus , 2022, 40 modules steel alloy, mirror panels, line. Courtesy Ruth Benzacar Galeria de Arte.

Exciting newcomers to the fair include Cecilia Brunson Projects (London), Nova Contemporary (Bangkok), and Ruth Benzacar Galeria de Arte (Buenos Aires) in the GALLERIES Sector; MISA SHIN GALLERY (Tokyo) in the FOCUS Sector; °CLAIRbyKahn (Zurich) and Boccanera Gallery (Trento, Milan) in FOCUS FIRST; Chilli (London), Danfe Arts (Kathmandu), and Galeri Ruang Dini (Bandung) in FUTURES; and EXHIBIT320 (New Delhi) in South Asia Insights, expanding the fair’s international scope and program, while others such as SPURS Gallery (Beijing), BAIK Jakarta (Jakarta, Seoul, Los Angeles), and Sabrina Amrani (Madrid) return after a one-year hiatus.

Established galleries from Southeast Asia returning to the fair include Ames Yavuz (London, Singapore, Sydney); STPI (Singapore); Sullivan+Strumpf (Singapore, Sydney, Melbourne); Richard Koh Fine Art (Singapore, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur); The Drawing Room (Manila); Gajah Gallery (Singapore, Jakarta, Yogyakarta, Manila); FOST Gallery (Singapore); Yeo Workshop (Singapore); and Haridas Contemporary (Singapore), offering a snapshot of the ideas and perspectives shaping contemporary art across the region today.
NARESH KUMAR ,

Long Way Home I (Gandhi & Kasturba II) , 2025–26, indigo, watercolor pencil, mica powder, marble dust, copper dust, and graphite on Mumbai Yellow Pages magazines in 53 panels, 176 x 196 cm. Courtesy Chilli.

S.E.A. Focus , commissioned by the National Arts Council and co-presented by ART SG for the second consecutive year. Curated by John Z.W. Tung, with artistic consultation from Emi Eu, its ninth edition takes “Better Worlds” as its curatorial theme, considering how technology, exchange, and human connection shape contemporary life.

The presentation brings together established artists from across the Southeast Asian region including Rirkrit Tiravanija, Vasan Sitthiket, and Tammy Nguyen alongside emerging practitioners such as Ida Lawrence, Weng Rajaie, and Siew Guang Hong. Malaysian artist Noor Azizan Rahman Paiman will present Putar Alam Cafe , an interactive work first commissioned for the 2016 Singapore Biennale, which invites visitors to engage directly with the artist through the familiar social rituals of eating and conversation.
ANDY DEWANTORO ,
The Sun, The Moon, The Raindrops Too , 2026, oil on canvas, 300 x 200 cm. Courtesy Galeri Ruang Dini.

What Is Worth Keeping, and What Is Left Behind? is a new commission by Singaporean artist Kray Chen presented in PLATFORM, ART SG’s sector for large-scale installations and performance. The expanded and reimagined participatory installation transforms bracelet-making into a negotiation between desire, chance, labor, and access. Building on its earlier presentation at Light to Night Singapore 2025, the installation extends Chen’s sustained interest in bodily behavior and the systems that organize everyday life.
DAWN NG ,
The Last Sunset . Courtesy of the artist.
KRAY CHEN ,
A Little Bead of Work , 2026, at the Light to Night Festival, Singapore Art Week, January 2025. Courtesy the artist.

For the first time, FILM will take place within the fair, presented on a large-format, double-sided 4 by 4-meter LED screen. The program brings together a compelling selection of moving-image works with the presentation of a major screen as a public art installation, animating a prominent public space and inviting visitors to experience film on an immersive scale.

Expanding FILM beyond the fair grounds, the world premiere of Dawn Ng’s The Last Sunset will be presented as a one-night-only, live cinema performance on Friday (January 22, 2027) at Filmhouse. The 30-minute event is a pairing of Ng’s monumental moving-image work with an original score by Welsh composer Alex Mills, and accompanied by a live choir within the audience.

PINAREE SANPITAK , Confess and Conceal , 2026, acrylic, pencil, silver leaf on canvas, 250 x 220 cm. Courtesy the artist and Ames Yavuz (left); and WAHIDA AHMED , Qaida , 2021, rice paper, ink, glue, and acrylic on canvas, 71 x 48 inches. Courtesy EXHIBIT320 (right).

ART SG will present How We Hold What’s Possible — Movement II as part of its offsite program in 2027, a major immersive project by acclaimed Thai artist Pinaree Sanpitak, curated by Artspace Executive Director Victor Wang. Presented in partnership with Artspace (Sydney), with Presenting Partner T:>Works and support from the National Arts Council, the project transforms 72-13, a heritage former rice warehouse, into a living environment exploring nourishment, rest and gathering from January 21–31 (opening January 20).

ART SG 2027 takes place from January 22–24, 2027, with a VIP Preview and Vernissage on January 21, at Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention. Tickets include access to S.E.A. Focus. Further information is available at artsg.com and seafocus.sg .
